title: Turnover Is the Real Expense in Field Marketing
content:
###  **Wages Are Predictable — Turnover Is Not** 

An hourly wage is easy to plan around. Turnover is not, and it is almost always the larger number by the end of a season. 

###  **Where the Cost Actually Lands** 

When a field hire leaves after three weeks, the wages paid are the smallest part of the loss. The training investment goes with them. The territory sits uncovered until a replacement is found. The recruiting process restarts. And whatever momentum was building in those neighborhoods stops. 

###  **Why Field Roles Turn Over So Quickly** 

Field work filters people fast. Someone who took the job for the schedule or the pay rate, without genuinely wanting the work itself, usually knows within two weeks that it is not a fit. That is not a failure of management — it is a predictable outcome of hiring for availability. 

###  **The Structural Difference** 

Turnover does not disappear in our model — it is simply our problem rather than a client's. When a representative is not working out, replacing them is handled on our end, and territory coverage continues without a gap. 

A client sees consistent weekly activity. What it took to keep it consistent is not their expense to absorb.
